Worked example: a weak and a strong analysis (simile)

The same device and the same sentence beginnings. Only the ideas after the beginnings make the difference.

✗ Weak

Cisneros states, “Your heart puffed and flowered like sheets drying on a line.” The verb “flowered” is significant because it is a nice word. Cisneros compares the heart to sheets to suggest something about the poem. She also emphasizes feelings. The reader is happy because it is nice. They also realize it is important. Through the use of a simile, Cisneros presents life.

  • The word is not explained: “a good word” could be said about any word.
  • “Something about the poem” and “feelings” could fit any poem.
  • “Sad because it is sad” gives no reason from the words, and “life” is not a message.
✓ Strong

Cisneros states, “Your heart puffed and flowered like sheets drying on a line.” The verb “flowered” is significant because it suggests the cloud's heart opened up happily, like a flower blooming. Cisneros compares the cloud's heart to sheets drying on a line to suggest that it feels light, soft and free. She also emphasizes the joy of an ordinary, everyday moment. The reader is cheerful because the image is so light and homely. They also realize that beauty can be found in simple, everyday moments. Through the use of a simile, Cisneros presents the lightness and joy of the cloud's free, ever-changing life.

  • Step 4 explains what the word suggests in THIS poem.
  • The device frame says exactly what the device shows in this poem.
  • The feeling has a reason that comes from the words, and the link gives a clear message.
The introduction (in the exam, it is given)

① Choose 2 devices that directly connect to the thesis in the introduction. Choose smartly.
  • The thesis is the last sentence: everything in the world is connected and always changing, and the cloud's freedom is something precious that not everyone can share.
  • A strong pair: one device about the cloud's many past lives (lines 1–26) and one about the prisoners watching it (lines 27–31).

Reminders
  • Cisneros is a woman: write she or Cisneros, never “he.”
  • Copy quotations exactly and put them inside quotation marks.
  • In step 4, zoom in on ONE word and name its word class first: “The adjective “___” is …” or “The noun “___” is …”.
  • Each box gets a gold star when every part of its structure is there. The ticks check structure; the 💡 hints help with ideas.
Finish

    Exam practice · 40 minutes

    Like the real exam, the poem has no highlights. Picture it, then write it: read the introduction, tap TWO lines of the poem where you see a device and name them, picture what each one shows, then write ONE body paragraph in your exam structure.

    While you write: your paragraph score (out of 100) goes up live. Naming the device, copying exact words and explaining them count most. Coach messages appear in the bar at the top, so they never cover your writing. Read each one, then keep writing.

    The timer keeps running if you leave the page. When time is up, your paragraph is checked automatically.
